title: Protocol to analyze transmigration of human cytotoxic T cells under physiological flow conditions in vitro
protocol: Calculate shear stress using the formula τ = η ⋅ 176.1 ⋅ Φ for μ-channel VI 0.4 system.
Set a flow rate of 0.8 mL/min on the pump to achieve 1 dyne/cm² of shear stress in the μ-channels.
Prepare the flow system according to the requirements for physiological conditions.
Connect inflamed monolayer containing μ-channels to the pump system.
Flow HEPES buffer through the system for equilibration.
Fill inlets connected to the liquid container until a meniscus forms at the top (1–2 mm high).
Hold the flow system Luer connector upside down and fill it with buffer to remove excess air.
Place the μ-channel containing inflamed endothelial monolayers on a microscope with phase contrast imaging.
Fix the slide to a sample holder and ensure it is securely attached.
Remove the lid, covering all but the channel to be used for imaging.
Connect the flow tubing from the pump to the channel slide, including clamps.
Unlock the clamps and connect one side of the tubing to the pump.
Connect the other end of the tubing to the liquid container.
Flush the tubing with 50 mL water, followed by 50 mL PBS, and then 50 mL HEPES+ at a high flow rate of 10 mL min-1.
Clamp the tubing on both sides after flushing.
Apply excess volume to the μ-channel inlet chambers of the channel to be imaged.
Remove the connective tubing.
Connect the Luer connectors from the pump and container side to the channel.
Flush excess air out of the Luer connector using a 200 µL pipette tip placed facing up.
Flush endothelial cells with HEPES+ buffer at approximately 0.7 dyne cm² for at least 10 minutes.
Avoid air bubble inclusion during connection of the liquid container side Luer connector.
Fill Luer outlets with a 200 μL pipette tip and HEPES+ buffer to remove excess air before connecting.
Tap air out of the syringe carefully before injecting.
Image series of CTL flown over the inflamed monolayer of endothelial cells are recorded microscopically.
Use phase contrast for quantitative analysis with 10× or 20× objectives.
Record images in higher detail using fluorescent labels for CTL and HUVEC at higher magnification.
Prepare 1 mL of CTL at 1 × 10^6 cells/mL in RPMI or HEPES+.
Use microscope software to save several positions randomly on the channel connected to the flow system.
Focus and use an auto-focus function if available.
Test positions, lighting, and focus settings by running the series for 2 or 3 rounds.
Inject CTL from the syringe slowly into the injection port located within the liquid container side tubing.
Match pump speed to achieve a flow rate of approximately 0.5 mL per minute.
Start a live image and follow a position near the inlet from the liquid container.
Start recording once CTL begin “raining” into the live frame.
Record for 15–30 minutes at intervals of 5–10 seconds.
Maintain focus throughout recording, ideally using an auto-focus solution.
Troubleshoot CTL activity and HUVEC inflammatory response if no transmigration is observed after 15 minutes.
Open saved image series in ImageJ.
Prepare an excel file for data analysis.
Use the ImageJ counting tool to count adherent and transmigrated cells in different groups.
Save the counts in an excel file.
Follow each cell individually from adhesion through the timeline.
Visually identify transmigrated cells by changes in phase contrast.
Mark the cells' transmigration spot using the counting tool.
Ensure that cells are truly transmigrated and not just flattened.
Follow each transmigrated CTL individually to confirm proper transmigration.
Determine how many EC:EC junctions a transmigrated cell passed before transmigration.
Count the number of adherent rounded CTL cells.
Calculate the frequency of unpolarized cells using the formula: (# of unpolarized rounded cells / # of adherent cells) * 100.
Determine the frequency of polarized but not transmigrated cells using the formula: ((# of adherent cells - # of transmigrated cells - # of unpolarized cells) / # of adherent cells).
Calculate the transmigration efficiency using the formula: (number of transmigrated cells / number of adherent cells) * 100.
Determine the frequency of distant diapedesis using the formula: (number of distantly transmigrated cells / number of transmigrated cells) * 100.
Transcellular route frequency: Calculate the percentage of transcellular events relative to local migration events multiplied by 100.
Paracellular route frequency: Subtract the calculated transcellular route frequency from 100% to determine paracellular route frequency.
Follow cells over the whole time course if they change contrast.
Carefully observe cell contrast as flattened untransmigrated CTL show inhomogeneous contrast while transmigrated CTL show homogeneously dark contrast.
Follow CTL over the whole time course to identify changes in morphology and contrast during migration.
